Posterior probability of a safety signal under the LL_BERN model

Source: R/llbern_post.R
llbern_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the relative risk under the log-logistic Bernoulli (LL_BERN) mixture model of Duncan (2026), which allows the hazard of the event to change over time.

Usage

llbern_post(
  y,
  t,
  k = 1,
  mu_hp,
  sigma_hp,
  pt_hp,
  df_p = 1,
  mu_d_prior = c(mu_hp, 1),
  sigma_d_prior = c(sigma_hp, 1),
  t_star,
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Vector of event indicators (1 if the subject had at least one occurrence of the event during follow-up, 0 otherwise).

t

Vector of follow-up times (positive), in the time unit for which mu_hp and sigma_hp were estimated.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to placebo (k:1).

mu_hp

Location parameter \(\mu\) of the log-logistic distribution estimated from historical placebo data (positive).

sigma_hp

Scale parameter \(\sigma\) of the log-logistic distribution estimated from historical placebo data (positive).

pt_hp

Total patient time of the historical placebo population.

df_p

Discount factor for the historical placebo data.

mu_d_prior

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior for \(\mu_d\); the default is c(mu_hp, 1).

sigma_d_prior

Shape and rate of the Gamma prior for \(\sigma_d\); the default is c(sigma_hp, 1).

t_star

Time at which the relative risk and the cumulative incidences are evaluated.

rr0

Critical value of the relative risk.

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible interval of the relative risk.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles of \(RR(t^*)\) are not computed (faster; used in sim_oc).

control

List of settings for the numerical integration: n_coarse (cells per coordinate of the coarse grid, default 12), n_outer (Gauss-Legendre nodes per coordinate, default 16), n_inner (Chebyshev points, default 121), check (default TRUE), eps (default 1e-8) and max_iter (default 12).

Value

An object of class bssd_post; see bdribs_post. The element model is "LL_BERN", rr summarizes \(RR(t^*)\), estimates contains the posterior means of \(\mu_p\), \(\sigma_p\), \(\mu_d\) and \(\sigma_d\), and integration contains the nodes used and the error estimate.

Details

For subject \(i\) with follow-up time \(t_i\), the model is $$P(Y_i = 1) = w_p F(t_i; \mu_p, \sigma_p) + w_d F(t_i; \mu_d, \sigma_d),$$ where \(F\) is the log-logistic cumulative incidence (ll_cdf), \(w_p = 1 / (k + 1)\) and \(w_d = k / (k + 1)\). The priors are $$\mu_p \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(PT_{HP} \mu / DF_p, PT_{HP} / DF_p), \quad \sigma_p \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(PT_{HP} \sigma / DF_p, PT_{HP} / DF_p),$$ $$\mu_d \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\mu, 1), \quad \sigma_d \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\sigma, 1),$$ with shape and rate parameters, where \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) are the historical placebo values (mu_hp and sigma_hp). The priors for the study drug parameters can be changed with mu_d_prior and sigma_d_prior.

Duncan (2026) does not state which relative risk is used for the signal criterion of this model. This function uses the ratio of the cumulative incidences at the time t_star, $$RR(t^*) = F(t^*; \mu_d, \sigma_d) / F(t^*; \mu_p, \sigma_p),$$ and declares a signal when \(P[RR(t^*) > rr_0 \mid \mathrm{data}] > \) cutoff.

The four-dimensional posterior is integrated numerically on the coordinates \(\log \mu_p\), \(\log \sigma_p\), \(\log \mu_d\) and the prior distribution function of \(\sigma_d\); the last one keeps the heavy left tail of the prior of \(\sigma_d\) under control. A coarse grid first locates the region that holds all but control$eps of the posterior mass in each marginal. On that region, Gauss-Legendre quadrature is used for three coordinates and Chebyshev interpolation for \(\log \mu_d\). Since \(RR(t^*) > rr_0\) holds exactly when \(\mu_d\) is below a value determined by the other three parameters, the posterior probability and the quantiles of \(RR(t^*)\) are obtained from the cumulative integral of the interpolant without a discontinuous integrand. When control$check is TRUE, the computation is repeated with about 1.25 times as many Gauss-Legendre nodes and 1.5 times as many Chebyshev points, the finer result is returned, and twice the absolute difference in prob between the two results is reported as the integration error estimate.

When there are few events, the prior of \(\sigma_d\) used by Duncan (2026) puts much mass near zero, where the likelihood changes sharply in \(\mu_d\) near the logarithms of the follow-up times. The integration error then decreases only in proportion to the inverse of the number of Chebyshev points, and its sign changes irregularly. With 1.5 times as many points, the error of the finer result is then about twice the difference between the two results, which is the reason for the factor 2 in the error estimate. The default number of Chebyshev points is large for the same reason, and the error estimate is not reliable when control$n_inner is much smaller than the default. If the reported error estimate is too large for the purpose, increase control$n_inner.

The posterior mean of \(RR(t^*)\) can be unstable because its posterior distribution may have a heavy right tail; the posterior median is a more stable summary.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

ll_cdf, ll_mu, expbern_post

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 60
t <- runif(n, 4, 104)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, ll_cdf(t, mu = 6.5, sigma = 0.8))
fit <- llbern_post(y, t, k = 1, mu_hp = 6.5, sigma_hp = 0.8, pt_hp = 200,
                   t_star = 104, control = list(check = FALSE))
fit
#> Model: LL_BERN 
#> Relative risk: ratio of cumulative incidences at t_star = 104 
#> P(RR(t_star) > 1 | data) = 0.2741
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of RR(t_star): mean 0.7703, median 0.1454, 95% interval (1.012e-119, 4.212)
#> Cumulative incidence at t_star = 104: placebo 0.09706, study drug 0.06457, difference -0.03249
